requirements.requirement: Forward node2 inventory log messages to node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: An inventory-tagged message generated on node2 traversed an established TCP connection and appeared in the required file on node1. An unrelated tagged message was excluded. Final observations show valid configurations, active and enabled rsyslog services, the collector listening, an established sender connection, and all test records retained in the required file.

requirements.requirement: Keep log forwarding and persistence working after either node1 or node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Both nodes had healthy pre-restart states, acknowledged restart requests, became temporarily unreachable, returned with different boot IDs, and recovered rsyslog. A new node2 inventory message was successfully persisted after the node1 restart, and another was successfully persisted after the node2 restart. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Inventory-tagged messages flowed from node2 to node1 and were persisted at the required path, while unrelated messages were filtered. Direct bounded restart transitions on both managed nodes demonstrated service recovery and successful post-restart message delivery. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle observations.
limitations: End-to-end behavior was tested with synthetic logger records tagged as inventory rather than output observed from a separately running inventory application process.
The evidence demonstrates resumed delivery after each restart but does not specifically exercise queued-message replay for messages emitted while node1 was offline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Chronological review found that collector configuration, directory creation, SELinux relabeling, restricted firewall setup, sender configuration, and rsyslog restarts directly established the requested outcome. Synthetic log writes were bounded functional and filtering evidence, while both scheduled reboots were required task and provider-protocol tests. No mutation required reversal, and no unwanted residue was observed. Final snapshots show healthy package state, no failed services, and only the required collector socket added; reboot-created systemd temporary directories are normal lifecycle changes.
